translationRepairs: Yin memorialized; Zhaozong refused. Days later the Founder asked again. Zhu Wen said: “I would never dare raise a hand—Yin is trying to sell me out.”
Yin memorialized; Zhaozong refused. Another day Zhaozong asked the Founder about it. Zhu Wen said: “I would never dare raise a hand—Yin is trying to sell me out.”
佗日以問太祖 continues from 昭宗不許, so Zhaozong asked Taizu; 太祖曰「臣安敢及之」 is a servant’s reply to the emperor. The prior “the Founder asked again” reverses asker and addressee.
Yin memorialized it; Zhaozong would not consent. Another day the Founder asked again. The Founder said: “How would your servant dare touch this? Yin means to sell me out.”
Yin memorialized it; Zhaozong would not consent. Another day he asked the Founder. The Founder said: “How would your servant dare touch this? Yin means to sell me out.”
以問太祖 marks Taizu as the one questioned; the zero subject carries from 昭宗不許. “The Founder asked again” invents the wrong agent.
At the move to Luoyang Zhaozong told Jiang Xuanhui: “De is my beloved son. Why does Quanzhong want him dead?”
At the move to Luoyang Zhaozong told Jiang Xuanhui: “The Prince of De is my beloved son. Why does Quanzhong want him dead?”
德王 is the title Prince of De; clipping to “De” drops the enfeoffment title Zhaozong uses for his son.

Eunuch Liu Jishu plotted to depose Zhaozong. His nephew Xiyin came through embassy clerk Cheng Yan to Zhen: “The emperor has turned cruel and kills without cause. The chief eunuch fears for his neck and will depose him. Will you and the clerks act together to settle the court—yes or no?”

Eunuch Liu Jishu plotted to depose Zhaozong. His nephew Xizheng came through embassy clerk Cheng Yan to Zhen: “The emperor has turned cruel and kills without cause. The chief eunuch fears for his neck and will depose him. Will you and the clerks act together to settle the court—yes or no?”
希正 romanizes as Xizheng; Xiyin does not match the characters.

The Founder was fighting between Xing and Ming. Jishu forged a retired-emperor edict to him. Zhu Wen wavered. Zhen said: “The disorders of Shufan and Yili became the stuff from which hegemons are made.

The Founder was fighting between Xing and Ming. Jishu forged a retired-emperor edict to him. Zhu Wen wavered. Zhen said: “The disorders of Shu Diao and Yili became the stuff from which hegemons are made.
豎刁 is the Qi eunuch Shu Diao; Shufan is a mistransliteration that breaks the Spring-and-Autumn allusion.
When Pei Ji of the Works ran the Finance Commission he took Di as touring inspector.
When Pei Qu of the Works ran the Finance Commission he took Di as touring inspector.
裴璩 is Pei Qu; Ji does not correspond to 璩.

Fan delivered Zongquan to Zhu Wen. The Founder wanted the triumph loud and asked to present the captive at Tang court. Tang answered that Shi Pu, when he broke Huang Chao, had sent only severed ears—Zongquan was not worth a grand presentation. Remonstrance official Xu Yanqiu also asked that he be executed on the spot.

Fan delivered Zongquan to Zhu Wen. The Founder wanted the triumph loud and asked to present the captive at Tang court. Tang answered that Shi Pu, when he broke Huang Chao, had sent only severed ears—Zongquan was not worth a grand presentation. Remonstrance official Xu Yanshu also asked that he be executed on the spot.
徐彥樞 ends in 樞 (shu); Yanqiu misreads the given name.

Taizu feared the warlords would turn on him while he was weak. He nudged Du Hong, Zhong Chuan, Wang Shinan, Qian Liu, and the rest to name him commander-in-chief and to let him hold Yan Prefecture as well.

Taizu feared the warlords would turn on him while he was weak. He nudged Du Hong, Zhong Chuan, Wang Shifan, Qian Liu, and the rest to name him commander-in-chief and to let him hold Yan Prefecture as well.
王師範 is Wang Shifan; Shinan is a wrong romanization of 範.
He was orphaned early and wound up in Bian Prefecture. A wealthy man named Li Ranglan bought him in the slave market and raised him as his own.
He was orphaned early and wound up in Bian Prefecture. A wealthy man named Li Rang obtained him and raised him as his own.
李讓 is the personal name and 闌得之 the verb phrase “obtained him”; Li Ranglan and “bought him in the slave market” fuse and invent beyond the Chinese.
When Taizu held Xuanyi he adopted Li Rang. Xun took the Zhu surname for himself.
When Taizu held Xuanwu he adopted Li Rang. Xun took the Zhu surname for himself.
宣武 is Xuanwu Circuit; Xuanyi misreads 武.

Later Liang attacked Wu and Pang Shigu fell at Qingkou. Broken troops straggled home through Ying in blinding snow, starving and freezing. Jingrao stacked firewood along the Huai and cooked porridge for them; many lived because of it. Taizu named him acting governor of Wuning, then military commissioner.

Afterwards Liang troops attacked Wu and Pang Shigu fell at Qingkou. Broken troops straggled home through Ying in blinding snow, starving and freezing. Jingrao stacked firewood along the Huai and cooked porridge for them; many lived because of it. Taizu named him acting governor of Wuning, then military commissioner.
其後 is temporal “afterwards,” and 梁兵攻吳 names Liang troops; “Later Liang” wrongly treats 其後梁 as the dynasty 後梁.

Ying bordered Huainan West and Qin Zongquan struck again and again. Jingrao fought him off. Zongquan swallowed every Henan prefecture but could not take Ying, and people from the surrounding districts fled to Jingrao for safety.

Ying bordered Huaixi (Huai West) and Qin Zongquan struck again and again. Jingrao fought him off. Zongquan swallowed every Henan prefecture but could not take Ying, and people from the surrounding districts fled to Jingrao for safety.
淮西 is Huaixi (Huai West), distinct from 淮南; Huainan West conflates the two circuits.
